metadata.title: OpenEconomy reported-data graph
metadata.warning: Reported-data view. Only source systems already integrated are shown. Missing edges mean not yet integrated, not zero. BLS QCEW payroll and FEC federal campaign-finance aggregates are currently live; BEA, Fed, SEC, Census, Treasury, USAspending and transaction-level FEC data are being added source by source.

entities.name: Political Funding Sources
entities.description: Aggregate funding sources reported to federal political committees. This is a source-category placeholder until transaction-level donor/entity resolution is loaded.

entities.name: Federal PACs
entities.description: Federal political action committees filing with the FEC, including separate segregated funds and nonconnected committees.

entities.name: Super PACs
entities.description: Independent-expenditure-only political committees. They may receive unlimited contributions but may not contribute directly to candidates.

entities.name: Party Committees
entities.description: National, state and local federal political party committees filing with the FEC.

entities.name: Congressional Candidate Committees
entities.description: House and Senate candidate committees with financial activity in the 2025-2026 cycle.

entities.name: Political Spending Recipients
entities.description: Vendors and other persons receiving political committee disbursements. Transaction-level FEC files will resolve this aggregate into named payees.

entities.name: Independent-Expenditure Vendors
entities.description: Payees receiving independent-expenditure payments. Candidate support/opposition is not a money transfer and will be modeled separately.

flows.note: Private-sector QCEW total annual wages. Covers 133,160,274 annual-average jobs across 11,806,967 establishments. Gross covered wages are not the same measure as BEA compensation of employees.
Federal, state, and local QCEW wages combined: $307.040B federal + $411.180B state + $1,008.815B local.

2,236 independent-expenditure-only political committees reported $1.7246B in receipts. The aggregate does not identify donor sectors; transaction-level individual and committee receipt files will resolve the source side.

Super PAC total disbursements through March 31, 2026. This includes multiple spending categories and must not be added to independent expenditures as if independent expenditures were separate spending.
PAC contributions to federal candidates totaled $274.5M. Independent-expenditure-only committees are prohibited from making candidate contributions.

$252.1M of independent expenditures were reported across Super PACs, hybrid PACs, other PACs, other persons and parties. The money edge terminates at vendors/payees; support or opposition to a candidate is a separate semantic relation.
